_schema.passes: true | false | "blocked" — three states, because reality has three. `true` means every step was observed to pass. `false` means it failed or has not been attempted. `"blocked"` means the step is correct and this environment cannot execute it — a headless browser that cannot emulate a media query, a CI run that only fires on a pull request, a clipboard that needs real user activation. Recording those as `true` with an apology in `notes` is the exact fudge invariant 2 exists to prevent, and it is what happened before this field had a third state.
_schema.blocked_reason: Required when passes is "blocked". What specifically could not be observed, and why — the limitation, not the feature.
_schema.recheck_when: Required when passes is "blocked". The condition under which this becomes verifiable: 'a real browser with reduced motion enabled', 'once a PR is open'. Stage 4 collects these; a blocked feature with no recheck condition is an abandoned one.
_schema.notes: What was observed. Not what was intended.
_schema.phases: One phase (or sprint) per branch is the default. Cut at Stage 2 BEFORE the features, grouping by contract dependency first — if a feature here reads a field, state shape, DOM node, token, route, or event another phase produces, they are one phase — and by shared premise only among what the contract test leaves free. Never group by subject matter. Sub-branches below the phase level are optional and each must have its reason written in progress.md.
_schema.phase.branch: Two phases MAY share a branch value, but only as a deliberate compression of phases the dependency test found independent, and knowing it costs rollback resolution. The phases stay as separate rows either way — a compression is a branching decision, not a re-plan, so never delete a phase to match the branch count.
_schema.phase: Required on every feature — which phase owns it. A feature with no phase means the phase plan was skipped; add the phase rather than a null.
_schema.phase.demonstrable: What a person can be shown at the end of this phase, and say yes or no to. A phase whose outcome cannot be demonstrated cannot be UAT'd either, and is usually a layer masquerading as a phase.
_schema.phase.premise: The assumption the phase's features rest on. When it expires, the blast radius is this phase — that is the reason to group by premise.
_schema.phase.status: planned | in_progress | merged | abandoned. `abandoned` is recorded, never deleted: a dropped phase is a decision, and invariant 1 supersedes decisions in place.
_schema.phase.merged_at: The merge commit sha. This is what makes the phase revertable as a unit and what a sprint report is later built from. Null until merged.
